accepted: P and PN share static normal_gate. Only runtime n_intercept differs.
A bank with an accepted translation waits in AWAIT_RESP with ready=1; arbitrary sustained fast-response backpressure is not a demonstrated production path.
The measured late-probe TL overlap effect is small in 52 enumerated scenarios.
A completion events are independent lane events; same-window rate interpretation only.

rejected_or_narrowed.claim: All additional board time must be outside TL.
rejected_or_narrowed.reason: 52 single-pair synthetic timing cases do not exhaust TL behavior or prove a board-wide bound.

rejected_or_narrowed.claim: Response arbiter input index0 is fast and all runs begin fast-priority.
rejected_or_narrowed.reason: Packed concatenation {fast_resp_data, slow_resp_data} maps index0=slow, index1=fast; warm-up also evolves RR state. No need to rely on assumed fixed bias.

rejected_or_narrowed.claim: Recover A-done interarrival intervals from aggregate p4m.window[3].
rejected_or_narrowed.reason: A-done total alone contains no per-event timestamps.

rejected_or_narrowed.claim: Build a new banked DMA test from scratch.
rejected_or_narrowed.reason: Existing tests/nonblock_actual_dma* already instantiate real banked controller/TL/iDMA; reuse and scope policy/runtime parameters. Current runner only exposes s/n and disables policy.

conclusion: No verified RTL fault explaining current ~896k-cycle PN regression. Keep actual DMA/data-path scheduling and shared ingress AW wait as priorities, not established root cause.
